WICKLOW COUNTY COUNCIL TO BENEFIT IN THE REGION OF €50M UNDER THE HOUSING INFRASTRUCTURE 
INVESTMENT FUND 
Wicklow County Council welcomes the announcement made earlier today from the Department of Housing, Local 
Government and Heritage of funding allocated to infrastructure projects supported in the first phase of the Housing 
Infrastructure Investment Fund (HIIF) programme. 
These projects are the first to be funded as part of a major multi-annual fund committed to unlocking land and 
enabling the delivery of housing at scale. These infrastructure projects will unlock housing in towns and cities across 
the country. 
Three projects across within County Wicklow will receive support through this first phase: 
• 
Rathnew Inner Relief Road, between €10m and €20m. Directly unlocks lands for 418 residential units and 
indirectly supports a further 186 residential units. 
• 
Fassaroe - Pedestrian & Cycle Bridge across N11/M11, Bray, < €10m. Bray MD and Environs LAP identifies 
capacity for 4,000 residential units in this area. The project also indirectly supports a further 3,000 residential 
units. 
• 
Fassaroe - Road Infrastructure N11 to Enniskerry, Bray > €20m. The Fassaroe LAP identifies capacity for 4,000 
residential units in this area. The project also indirectly supports a further 3,000 residential units 
Administered by the new Housing Activation Office within the Department of Housing, the €1 bn Housing 
Infrastructure Investment Fund is the largest housing infrastructure fund announced in Ireland for many years. 
The Housing Activation Office, will coordinate the multi-agency investment required at all levels, working directly with 
critical utilities and transport agencies, including Uisce Éireann and ESB Networks, to ensure that complementary 
investment is provided and that lands are fully serviced and ready to deliver housing. 
WICKLOW COUNTY COUNCIL WECOMES ALLOCATION OF €10.72 MILLION IN FUNDING FOR ROADS DAMAGED 
DURING STORM CHANDRA 
Wicklow County Council welcomes the recent announcement from the Department of Transport of €10.72m in 
funding allocated to address the damage caused to regional and local roads across the county by Storm Chandra 
earlier this year. 
Minister for Transport Darragh O’Brien and Ministers of State Seán Canney and Jerry Buttimer allocated the funding as 
part of an additional €40 million provided to local authorities to undertake necessary work to restore the road 
infrastructure damaged during the storm.

This includes, depending on house surveyed, and not limited to external wall insulation, attic insulation, heat pumps and

Addressing Homelessness in Partnership with Approved Housing Bodies 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – Kilmantin Hill, Wicklow 
Kilmantin Hill has 11 rooms to support persons either homeless, exiting a higher support facility, or in danger of becoming 
homeless.  
There are 10 clients supported in the Kilmantin Hill facility, operated by Dublin Simon. There is continuous transition by 
the clients to suitable alternative accommodation. 
A report is being undertaken at present to cost the refurbishment of the current rooms with a view to making them all 
ensuite. More details will be available over the coming months. 
Homeless Family Service – Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow   
Dublin Simon are engaged by Wicklow County Council to operate and manage the facility at Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow 
as a Family Homeless Service. The building comprises of three 1-bed units, two 2-bed units, and two 3-bed units.  
It is envisaged that families will avail of the service for circa 6-months STA (Supported Temporary Accommodation) with 
key working support to enable families to transition from homelessness into Homeless HAP, or alternative longer-term 
accommodation.   
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – San Remo, Bray 
San Remo is operated by Dublin Simon and incorporates a service model whereby there are a number of emergency/cold 
weather initiative beds and Supported Temporary Accommodation Beds (STA). There is on site key working support 
linking in with clients.    
The Neighbourhood Liaison Committee is now operational and meets monthly. 
Bi-monthly meetings are held with Dublin Simon and Wicklow County Council staff.

Homeless Supported Accommodation - Carraig Eden, Greystones 
This facility provides 35 ensuite bedrooms with associated kitchens and common areas and is fully operational. Wicklow 
County Council run an in-reach service with the clients to support them as they continue their journey into more permanent 
accommodation.  
Other Homeless Supported Accommodation 
Wicklow County Council owned properties in Wicklow, Bray, and Greystones, leased to Approved Housing Bodies, 
provide 12 units of low to medium supported accommodation targeted to the particular support needs of the clients. Six 
of these persons living in shared accommodation have now successfully moved into their forever homes and this in turn 
created space to move further people out of homelessness.  
A homeless outreach service has been rolled out in Bray and is proving very successful. 
Housing First 
Peter McVerry Trust has been appointed as the Housing First Programme Implementer for the Mid-East Region. Wicklow 
County Council is committed to working with them and has now reached and surpassed the targets identified in the 
programme. Housing First recognises that a stable home provides the basis for recovery in other areas.  
 
Properties will be provided by both Wicklow County Council and Peter McVerry Trust for the implementation of the 
programme. 
Wicklow County Council has, to date, successfully accommodated 19 clients under Housing First.  Other clients proposed 
for Housing First have been assessed by the team and are availing of key support work pending finalisation of sourcing 
of accommodation. The main issue facing this programme is the availability of 1-bed units in suitable locations with easy 
access to required services.

Community Awards Scheme (CAS) 2026 
As part of its commitment to supporting local community development, Wicklow County Council operates an annual 
Community Award Scheme. 
The fund for 2026 was available as grant aid to successful community groups and local organisations wishing to undertake 
community projects in their area.  
The maximum grant amount of €1,000.00 per organisation for small projects and group running costs. 
Payments of grants are issuing during July. 
      
Local Enhancement Programme (LEP) 2026 
This funding will provide capital supports that are essential for many small community groups and organisations, 
particularly those who serve disadvantaged communities in rural and urban areas. 
The scheme is designed to ensure local priorities are identified and met, to improve and enhance community facilities for 
all. Funding has been offered to a diverse range of community groups including, but not limited to, community centres, 
parish halls and local voluntary groups. 
The Wicklow Local Community Development Committee (LCDC) is responsible for allocating funding through this scheme 
and applications were required to link to one or more key priority areas identified in the Local Economic and Community 
Plan (LECP) to be eligible for consideration. 
The Department of Rural and Community Development and the Gaeltacht awarded €199,043.66 as part of the 2026 
Programme, and all successful applicants have now been notified of their award.  
Payments of grants will be made in the coming weeks.

incredible work happening in communities across Ireland. It celebrates the people who roll up their sleeves, work 
together, and make their local communities vibrant, welcoming, and inspiring places to live.

Social Farming 
Throughout the month of July, four placements will engage in the Social Farming project on Violet Kavanagh’s farm in

Period Poverty 
Deriving from the latest allocation of Period Dignity approved by the Department of Health, Healthy Wicklow has 
partnered with Wicklow Library Service to provide free period products in all 13 public libraries across County Wicklow. 
This initiative aims to improve access to essential menstrual products, promote period dignity, and help address period 
poverty by ensuring products are freely available in welcoming and accessible community spaces.

Croí Cónaithe (Towns, Cities and Rural) – Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant 
The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is a payment you can get if you are turning a vacant house or building into 
your permanent home or a rental property.  The grant applies to qualifying vacant properties in cities, towns, villages and 
rural parts of the country. 
There are 2 types of Grants available: 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant of up to €50,000 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant including the Derelict Property top up grant of up €70,000 
To qualify for the top up of €20,000, an independent report prepared by a Structural Engineer, along with a copy of their 
Professional Indemnity Insurance, is required to be submitted along with the application, confirming, to the satisfaction of 
the local authority, that the property is derelict i.e. structurally unsound and dangerous. 
To qualify for the grant, applicants must: 
Have proof of ownership or evidence of active negotiations to buy the property (that is, confirmation of engagement from 
the estate agent or owner of the property) where you are seeking approval in principle for a grant. 
- 
Live in the property as your principal private residence or make it available for rent. 
- 
Have proof that the property has been vacant for at least 2 years and that it was built up to and including 2007.

Information Systems 
 
Operations  
• 
The IT Helpdesk continues to streamline the workflow for the technical support team with an average of 50 tickets 
a day this month, providing assistance for both in-house and remote workers.  
 
GIS & Systems Analysis 
Property Portfolio Register 
• 
Work continued to support the development of the Council's Property Portfolio Register. Mapping and property 
datasets were prepared and shared to assist with the ongoing implementation of the new system. The project will 
provide a more comprehensive and accessible record of Council-owned assets. This will help improve property 
management and support future planning and decision-making. 
Expanding Automated GIS Workflows 
• 
Work continued on expanding automated GIS processes to improve the efficiency of data management. A new 
automated workflow was implemented to monitor updates to key datasets and process changes without manual 
intervention. These improvements reduce processing times and ensure information remains current.  
Supporting Emergency Response through GIS Collaboration with Coillte and Fire Service 
• 
A GIS collaboration initiative was progressed with Coillte and the Council’s Fire Service to improve access to 
mapping information for emergency response planning. Coillte demonstrated their GIS-based Fire Service 
application, showcasing how spatial information can support operational decision-making. Agreement was 
reached to establish an ArcGIS Online collaboration to facilitate secure sharing of relevant mapping data.  
Supporting Environmental Research through the EU Horizon Sponge Works Project 
• 
GIS support was provided to the EU Horizon Sponge Works Project through the preparation and delivery of high-
resolution elevation datasets for the Ovoca-Vartry Catchment and Avoca Subcatchment. Relevant Bluesky 
elevation data was processed and supplied to Trinity College Dublin to support ongoing research activities. This 
work supports research focused on environmental resilience and sustainable water management. 
Enhancing Digital Tools for Agricultural Inspections 
• 
Development work continued on the Council’s ArcGIS Survey123 application to support agricultural inspection 
activities. The inspection form was customised to meet Wicklow County Council’s specific operational 
requirements, including localised information relating to rainfall and crop-spreading periods. The updated digital 
workflow will improve the efficiency and consistency of inspection data collection.  
Infrastructure 
• 
Ongoing upgrades of WAN connections at remote sites by Wicklow County Council aim to optimize performance 
and cost-effectiveness.
